subject: Clarification: elastic seats, context reuse and minimum billing behavior
messages:
From: Bryan Cole <bryan@brightcart.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: 2028-07-10T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Question on minimums when seats spike

Hi Neha,

Quick question as we're finalizing our internal forecast: BrightCart has a pretty elastic usage pattern — baseline ~20 seats overnight, but we regularly spike to ~120 seats for a few hours mid-day for batch reprocessing. Our procurement team is asking whether Redwood's monthly minimums apply to the peak or the baseline, and how token/context reuse across seats is treated for billing.

Specific asks:
- If 100 seats are active for 3 hours only, are those counted against the monthly minimum?
- If multiple seats share the same conversation prefix (same customer session reused), do we get any prefix/KV reuse credit or is it per-seat token accounting?
- Can you provide a sample invoice for a month with this pattern?

Thanks — if it's easier we can schedule a quick call.

Bryan
Bryan Cole
Head of Product, BrightCart
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Bryan Cole <bryan@brightcart.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: 2028-07-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on minimums when seats spike

Hi Bryan — thanks for the clear summary. TL;DR: short bursts are metered/prorated but can interact with the monthly minimum quantum; prefix/KV reuse reduces token work but does not directly reduce the per-seat minimum unless the workload falls below the committed baseline. Attached is a working calculator (pricing_calc_v1.xlsx) — I'll inline the high-level rules below and then we can run your sample numbers.

High-level rules (short):
- Minimums are applied at the contract SKU level (commit slab) on a monthly cadence. If you commit to a baseline of N seats, the baseline minimum is billed regardless of short-term inactivity.
- Elastic or burst seats are billed as usage above baseline. For bursts within the same month we bill the incremental tokens used during those bursts; they are NOT automatically folded into the baseline unless you convert the burst into a committed seat in your next renewal.
- We prorate burst charges to the second and round token charges to our token quantum (1,000 token buckets for the current pilot SKU). That rounding can create small per-burst deltas — we illustrate in the sheet.
- Prefix/KV reuse: the runtime caches prefixes globally for the customer region/tenant. If multiple seats hit the same conversation prefix within the same cache window, compute cost is reduced (fewer decode tokens). However billing is still per-request tokens observed at the API layer after cache savings. In short, prefix reuse reduces billed tokens but does not collapse separate seat counts for minimum eligibility.

Next steps: if you send a small sample of your daily seat-time distribution (peak length + baseline), I can produce a sample invoice showing baseline minimums + burst usage line items and the rounding noise. I included a sample tab in pricing_calc_v1.xlsx showing 1000-token quantum rounding examples.

Would you be able to share a day or week of anonymized seat timelines (start/end in UTC)? If not, tell me a typical weekday profile and I'll model it.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Date: 2028-07-11T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on minimums when seats spike

Thanks Neha — sending a simplified CSV attached (sample_usage.csv). Example weekday: baseline 20 seats 00:00–08:00 and 20 seats 20:00–24:00, between 08:00–20:00 we ramp to 120 seats for roughly 4 hours and sit at ~60 seats the rest of the day. Peak burst windows are typically 2–4 hours.

One clarification: you mentioned rounding at 1,000-token buckets — is that per-request or per-invoice-line (we're trying to understand if many small requests inflate rounding). Also, would a prefix reuse scenario where a customer session is touched by 3 different seats in the same minute show up as three token requests (albeit many tokens served from cache) or as one consolidated event for billing?

Bryan

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Bryan Cole <bryan@brightcart.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-11T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on minimums when seats spike

Hi Bryan — looping in Sergio for a quick confirm on the mechanics and to propose a commercial approach. Two quick notes from our side:

1) Procurement signal: customers with elastic usage like this often prefer a committed baseline equal to their 75th percentile sustained seats + a burst buffer. That gives them predictable minimums while keeping burst elasticity. We can propose a baseline at 50 seats + burst billing.
2) Pilot concession: to remove friction, we're OK waiving the first month minimum on a 3-month pilot (we'll bill actual usage for bursts). After the pilot we can move to the committed baseline (and apply a committed-discount to the baseline).

Sergio — can you confirm we can waive month 1 baseline minimum and how that affects accounting (we need to track as a one-time credit)? Also legal asked whether the rounding quantum can be reduced for a pilot (from 1,000 to 250 tokens) to reduce rounding noise for low-latency small requests. Can we offer that as a pilot setting?

Bryan — if that sounds reasonable we'll produce a sample invoice with: baseline (committed seats) line, burst usage line (metered tokens), rounding adjustment line (if any), and a one-time pilot credit. Neha — can you produce that illustrative invoice using Bryan's sample_usage.csv and attach an updated sheet?

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Bryan Cole <bryan@brightcart.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-12T14:23:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice illustration + next steps (BRCH-4521)

Bryan / team — attached pricing_calc_v2.xlsx with a worked example using the CSV you provided. Key callouts from the worksheet (summary):

- Baseline commit suggested: 50 seats @ $1,200/seat-month (example committed price) = $60,000 baseline minimum.
- Burst usage (uplift above baseline): modeled tokens consumed across burst windows = 4,250,000 tokens for the month. After applying cache savings (modeled at 22% token reduction given your reuse patterns) billed burst tokens = 3,315,000 tokens.
- Token quantum rounding: with our 1,000-token quantum that becomes 3,316 buckets (round up) which inflates billed tokens by ~1,000 tokens (the rounding delta). If we reduce quantum to 250 tokens for the pilot the rounding delta drops to ~250 tokens. The sheet shows both columns.
- Sample illustrated invoice lines:
  • Line 1 — Baseline commit: $60,000 (committed seat minimum)
  • Line 2 — Burst usage: 3,316,000 tokens * $0.0008/token = $2,652.80
  • Line 3 — Rounding adjustment (pilot quantum 250): $0.20 (trivial in this example)
  • Line 4 — Pilot credit (waive month-1 baseline): -$60,000
  • Total due (pilot month): $2,653.00 (approx)

Actions:
- Bryan: confirm you want the 3-month pilot with month-1 baseline waived and pilot quantum set to 250 tokens. If yes I'll send a DocuSign addendum and we can lock pricing for the pilot period.
- Tessa / Sergio: confirm the one-time accounting credit approach and whether we need a special invoice memo for finance.

If helpful I can hop on a 30-minute call and walk through the worksheet and the assumptions (cache hit rate, seat mapping, token rate).

Thanks — attaching pricing_calc_v2.xlsx and the invoice mockup PDF.

—Neha
